title: Land Transport and Related Matters Bill, Second Reading debate
what_it_is: A Second Reading debate on the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill, an omnibus Bill by the Ministry of Transport and Ministry of Home Affairs that amends road traffic, active mobility, ERP 2.0, speed limiter and related laws.
why_it_matters: The Bill decriminalises missed ERP charges and makes the On-Board Unit mandatory for all Singapore-registered vehicles from 1 January 2027. It lowers the speed limit for mobility vehicles on public paths to six kilometres an hour from 1 June 2026, requires a Certificate of Medical Need for mobility scooter users on public paths, and introduces registration and penalties. It also raises penalties for illegal vehicle modifications and unregistered or deregistered vehicles, and updates speed limiter offences.

key_points.point: The Bill is an omnibus Bill regularising provisions across several existing Acts.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: The Land Transport and Related Matters Bill is an omnibus Bill that regularises provisions across several existing Acts.

key_points.point: Clauses 59 to 64 simplify settlement processes and decriminalise missed ERP charges.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: This is why we are introducing clauses 59 to 64 in this Bill to simplify settlement processes and to decriminalise missed ERP charges, which are currently an offence under the Road Traffic Act.

key_points.point: From 1 January 2027, the OBU will be mandatory for all Singapore-registered vehicles when ERP 2.0 is fully rolled out and ERP 1.0 is decommissioned.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: On 1 January 2027, when the ERP 2.0 is completely rolled out and ERP 1.0 is decommissioned, the OBU will be mandatory for all Singapore-registered vehicles.

key_points.point: Remaining vehicle owners get another three months to install OBUs at no cost.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: These vehicle owners, who have already been previously notified, will have another three months to install their OBUs at no cost.

key_points.point: Distance-based charging will not be introduced in the immediate term.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: This means that we will not be introducing distance-based charging in the immediate term.

key_points.point: Serious cases of deliberate non-compliance or misuse of OBUs carry penalties of up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment up to two years.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: For serious cases of deliberate non-compliance or misuse, the legislation provides for penalties of up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment of up to two years.

key_points.point: Clause 52 raises maximum penalties for illegal vehicle alterations.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: clause 52 of the Bill raises the maximum penalties for such illegal alterations.

key_points.point: Individuals can face fines up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment up to two years for illegal alterations, doubled for repeat offenders.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: Under the Bill, individuals can face fines up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, with penalties doubled for repeat offenders.

key_points.point: Clause 57 increases penalties for keeping or using unregistered or deregistered vehicles.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: Clause 57 of the Bill increases the penalties for offenders, who will face fines of up to $20,000, and/or jail of up to two years for the first offence, again with penalties doubled for repeat offenders.

key_points.point: The PMA rules are intended to take effect from 1 June 2026.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: To give stakeholders sufficient transition time after this Bill, we intend for the rules to take effect from 1 June 2026.

key_points.point: The speed limit for mobility vehicles on public paths will be lowered to six kilometres an hour.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: First, we will lower the speed limit for mobility vehicles on public paths to six kilometres an hour.

key_points.point: Dimension and weight limits will be introduced for PMAs used on public paths.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: Second, we will introduce dimension and weight limits for PMAs used on public paths.

key_points.point: Users of mobility scooters will need certification of medical need to ride on public paths.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: Third, we will require that users of mobility scooters be certified to have a medical need for the device, in order to ride a mobility scooter on public paths.

key_points.point: Mobility scooters must be checked for compliance and registered before sale.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: Fourth, we will also go upstream and require that mobility scooters are checked for compliance and registered before they are sold.

key_points.point: Existing mobility vehicles with device speed limit up to 10 km/h may be used on public paths until 31 December 2028, but must ride within 6 km/h.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: To ease the transition, we will allow existing mobility vehicles with a device speed limit of up to 10 kilometres per hour to be used on public paths until 31 December 2028, but they need to ride within the six kilometres per hour limit and meet all other rules.

key_points.point: From 1 January 2029, all mobility vehicles on public paths must have a device speed limit of six kilometres per hour and below.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: From 1 January 2029 onwards, all mobility vehicles used on public paths must have a device speed limit of six kilometres per hour and below.

key_points.point: From 1 June 2026, PMAs must not exceed width 70 cm, length 120 cm, height 150 cm and laden weight 300 kg.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: From 1 June 2026, PMAs must not exceed a width of 70 centimetres, a length of 120 centimetres, a height of 150 centimetres and a laden weight of 300 kilogrammes.

key_points.point: The Certificate of Medical Need will be available from 27 February 2026 through the AMS process.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: The certificate will be available later this month, from 27 February 2026, through the AMS process.

key_points.point: Seniors aged 70 and above are exempted from the certification requirement.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: Seniors aged 70 and above will be exempted from the certification requirement.

key_points.point: From 1 June 2026, mobility scooter users on public paths must have the Certificate of Medical Need.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: From 1 June 2026, mobility scooter users on public paths must have this Certificate of Medical Need.

key_points.point: Registration will start for mobility scooters sold from 1 June 2026.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: We will start by requiring registration for mobility scooters sold from 1 June 2026.

key_points.point: From 1 January 2029, all mobility scooters must be registered before use on a public path.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: Thereafter, from 1 January 2029, all mobility scooters will need to be registered before they can be used on a public path.

key_points.point: Keeping unsafe devices will be an offence.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: The Bill will make it an offence to keep such unsafe devices.

key_points.point: Speed limiter penalties increase to maximum fines of $10,000 for first conviction and $20,000 for subsequent convictions.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
key_points.quote: The Bill updates the penalty framework by increasing the maximum fines to $10,000 for a first conviction and $20,000 for subsequent convictions.

key_points.point: Owners and drivers will be liable for knowingly causing or permitting use of non-compliant speed limiter-required lorries and for tampering.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
key_points.quote: First, we will hold owners and drivers liable for knowingly causing or permitting the use of non-compliant speed limiter-required lorries and for tampering with installed speed limiters.

key_points.point: Authorised Agents will have a duty to report suspected tampering of a speed limiter.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
key_points.quote: Second, we will impose a duty on Authorised Agents to report suspected tampering of a speed limiter.

key_points.point: Courts may impose disqualification periods equal to or above the prescribed minimum, including lifetime disqualification.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
key_points.quote: The disqualification period that the Court may impose can be any period equal to or above the prescribed minimum disqualification period, including a lifetime disqualification period if it thinks fit.

key_points.point: Clauses 74 and 79 allow authorised civilians, including service providers, to process straightforward traffic violations subject to safeguards.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
key_points.quote: Clauses 74 and 79 amend the Road Traffic Act to allow processing of such violations to be carried out by authorised civilians, including service providers, subject to appropriate safeguards.

key_points.point: Forfeiture of road vehicles will be discretionary if the offender is not the owner and used the vehicle without the owner's consent.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
key_points.quote: The amendment will make the forfeiture of road vehicles discretionary in all scenarios if it is proved to the Court's satisfaction that the person who committed the scheduled offence involving the vehicle is not the vehicle owner and had used the vehicle without the consent of its owner.

key_points.point: Foreign-registered heavy vehicles are not required to install speed limiters because they also ply in other jurisdictions with different speed limits.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
key_points.quote: We do not require them to install speed limiters, because they also ply in other jurisdictions with different speed limits from Singapore.

key_points.point: Speeding-related accidents involving heavy vehicles decreased by 28% from 25 cases in 2024 to 18 cases in 2025.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
key_points.quote: The number of speeding-related accidents, including fatal ones, involving heavy vehicles has decreased by 28% from 25 cases in 2024 to 18 cases in 2025, as more lorries installed speed limiters last year.

key_points.point: MOH's position is that only doctors and OTs can assess and grant the Certificate of Medical Need.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: Hence, MOH's position is that only doctors and OTs can assess and grant this certificate.

key_points.point: The current cost of registering PABs is $50.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: As a comparison, the current cost of registering PABs is $50.

key_points.point: The registration framework will allow families to share a single mobility scooter.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: The registration framework will allow families to share a single mobility scooter.

key_points.point: LTA will use vehicle-specific ERP 2.0 data only for payment, charges and enforcement.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: As we have said before, LTA will use vehicle-specific data only for payment, charges and enforcement.

key_points.point: The OBU design is in line with the Federal Information Processing Standard level 4 security standard with cryptographic security keys.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: For example, the design of the OBU is in line with the Federal Information Processing Standard level 4 security standard with cryptographic security keys.

key_points.point: Old cars on the Classic or Vintage Vehicle schemes will be exempted from installing an OBU where technical problems cannot be resolved.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: Where technical problems cannot be resolved such as old cars on the Classic or Vintage Vehicle schemes, we will exempt them from the requirement to install an OBU.

key_points.point: Owners of such cars will pay a daily flat fee if they use their vehicles on ERP operational days.
key_points.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: Owners of such cars will then have to pay a daily flat fee if they use their vehicles on ERP operational days.

key_points.point: All lorries are expected to install speed limiters by 1 July 2027.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
key_points.quote: We expect these figures to further decrease after all lorries install speed limiters by 1 July 2027.

key_points.point: Enterprise Singapore expanded Productivity Solutions Grant support to cover speed limiters for eligible SMEs that install between 1 October 2025 and 31 March 2027.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
key_points.quote: To support SMEs, Enterprise Singapore has expanded Productivity Solutions Grant support to cover speed limiters for eligible SMEs that install between 1 October 2025 and 31 March 2027.

key_points.point: LTA will work with the Agency for Integrated Care and SG Enable and social service agencies to reach out to seniors and persons with disabilities.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: LTA will continue to work with the Agency for Integrated Care and SG Enable as well as relevant social service agencies, such as SPD, to reach out to seniors and persons with disabilities.

key_points.point: LTA's public communications campaign on the new rules will be rolled out in various languages.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: LTA's public communications campaign on the new rules will also be rolled out in various languages.

key_points.point: For delivery riders without mobility challenges, PMAs are not the right mode of transport.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: For delivery riders without mobility challenges, PMAs are not the right mode of transport for them.

key_points.point: They can continue their trade by switching to other devices or vehicles before 1 June 2026.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: They can continue their trade by switching to other devices or vehicles before 1 June 2026.

key_points.point: Platforms have committed to be inclusive in allocating jobs and providing earning opportunities for individuals with mobility challenges who rely on PMAs for delivery work.
key_points.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
key_points.quote: The platforms have committed to be inclusive in allocating jobs and providing earning opportunities for individuals from diverse backgrounds, including those with mobility challenges who rely on PMAs for their delivery work.

key_points.point: NDCA will provide financial assistance to subsidise and co-pay out-of-pocket compliance costs arising from the Act.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
key_points.quote: To support our members, the NDCA will provide financial assistance to help subsidise and co-pay out-of-pocket compliance costs arising from this Act.

key_points.point: Gho Sze Kee said it is time to hold platform companies more accountable for the safety of their workers and communities.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
key_points.quote: It is time to hold platform companies more accountable for the safety of their workers and the communities that they serve.

key_points.point: Edward Chia said ERP 2.0 is also a data and sensing platform.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
key_points.quote: At its core, ERP 2.0 is also a data and sensing platform.

key_points.point: Dennis Tan asked what encryption and anonymisation protocols apply to data transmitted from the OBU to the central server.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
key_points.quote: Can the Minister clarify what specific technical encryption and anonymisation protocols are applied to data transmitted from the OBU to the central server?

key_points.point: Eighteen PAP MPs will speak on PMAs, ERP 2.0, vehicle safety and related issues.
key_points.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
key_points.quote: A total of 18 PAP Members of Parliament (MPs) will speak on the new regulations on PMAs, ERP 2.0, vehicle safety and other related issues.
